title: Sources & maintenance
text: This public portal brings together Council research resources: assessment links, formatting tools, catch analyses, risk-table evidence, and SSC records. The topic pages link to existing public project websites and source repositories. GOA and BSAI time-series data and figures, their reproducible source, and the Tier 3 schematic are hosted here.

title: Sources & maintenance
text:
Scope and status
The original wiki was assembled on 24 September 2026. This public portal was prepared on 28 September 2026. Each linked analysis keeps its own date and scientific status. The ABC / TAC page explains the GOA and BSAI series, coverage, methods, and source revisions.

title: Tier 3 control rule
text: This figure shows how ABC and OFL fishing-mortality limits change with biomass. The axes express biomass and fishing mortality relative to MSY reference points, the values associated with maximum sustainable yield. The illustration uses the assumptions listed below.

title: Tier 3 control rule
text:
Assumptions in this figure
The script uses BMSY = B35, substitutes FMSY for F35, and assumes F40/FMSY = 0.75. The 0.75 ratio is an illustrative assumption; stock-specific Tier 3 ratios can differ. The script also assumes B35/B40 = 35/40 = 0.875 and sets alpha to 0.05 on the B/B40 scale.
With x = B/BMSY on the horizontal axis, both lines use this multiplier:
h(x) = max(0, min(1, (0.875*x - 0.05) / 0.95))
OFL line: F/FMSY = h(x)
ABC line: F/FMSY = 0.75*h(x)
The lines level off at x = 1/0.875, approximately 1.143. Fishing mortality reaches zero at x = 0.05/0.875, approximately 0.0571.

title: Tier 3 control rule
text:
Interpretation
The shaded regions carry the labels overfished, below BMSY, and overfishing under this figure’s assumptions. When applying a control rule, use reference points from the stock assessment and the applicable management specification.
Running the R script creates the PNG and PDF at 8.5 × 5.75 inches. The wiki displays that figure with its original assumptions.

title: ABC reduction
text: The main report compares BSAI and GOA groundfish risk-table scores with SSC reductions below maximum permissible ABC (maxABC) during 2018 to 2024. It explores the relationship through regressions and examples that translate risk scores into probabilities.

title: ABC reduction
text:
Evidence and interpretation
The risk-table data file contains 302 stock-year rows across 45 distinct stock labels. Completed risk tables account for part of this collection. The report’s regression analysis uses 21 quantified stock-year ABC reductions, entered by hand. It excludes years carried forward from previous advice and reductions without a stated amount.
Scoring conventions changed in 2019, 2023, and 2024. The report’s sensitivity analysis checks results after putting scores on a common scale. Consult this comparison when interpreting changes across years. The fitted relationships describe historical SSC behavior and remain exploratory.
The main report explores a proposal from the 2020 EBS Pacific cod assessment using assumed values for CV (coefficient of variation, a measure of relative uncertainty) and delta (position within the probability range assigned to a risk level). These scenarios are exploratory examples of a proposed decision rule.

title: SAFE audit
text: The SAFE audit collects assessment links from NPFMC and NOAA sources. Its tables help locate documents, examine stock coverage inferred from link details, and check inconsistent year labels or repeated filenames.

title: SAFE audit
text:
What is available
The saved catalog contains 1,326 records, 41 inferred stocks, and 32 effective years spanning 1984 to 2026, with gaps. Effective years are inferred from document labels and page context. Each record describes a link and inferred document details. Counting distinct, verified assessments would require a separate check. The saved anomaly table contains three records.

title: GOA and BSAI catch and harvest specifications
text:
Regional catch history, 2003–2025
The public AKFIN Economic SAFE report GFSAFE001 supplies the full 2003–2025 catch history available through that report for both regions. The source labels these data preliminary and reports a refresh date of 15 September 2026. Values include retained and discarded FMP groundfish catch, including groundfish caught while targeting halibut. The catch definition follows the source throughout this series.






Figure 1: Annual groundfish catch in separate BSAI and GOA panels, 2003–2025. Values come from the preliminary AKFIN Economic SAFE report GFSAFE001. Each vertical axis begins at zero.



The 2025 values are 1,794,251 metric tons for BSAI and 245,152 metric tons for GOA. These are the AKFIN series values. NOAA CAR110 totals, described below, use a different set of catch accounts.
PNG figure · SVG figure · Annual catch table · AKFIN public reports

title: GOA and BSAI catch and harvest specifications
text:
Harvest-specification history, from 1986
The ABC_TAC source project supplies 1986–2026 BSAI and 1986–2024 GOA records. This portal uses the full available history from those two source files at the linked revision. BSAI records use lag = 1 and OY = 1; GOA also uses Area = Total, which avoids adding area subtotals to their regional totals. The year is the year to which a specification applies.






Figure 2: BSAI and GOA annual TAC, ABC, and OFL from the public ABC_TAC compilation. BSAI records cover 1986–2026 and GOA records 1986–2024. Open circles identify sums containing missing source entries.



Specifications PNG · Specifications SVG · Full annual specifications table
Open circles identify sums with missing source entries. For example, the source contains one zero and 28 missing OFL entries for BSAI in 1991; the displayed zero preserves that source record and its partial coverage. This compilation supports examination of the historical series; regulatory totals and current limits should be checked against the cited NOAA records.
Missing source entries remain missing. Available entries are summed, and each downloadable annual record reports how many entries contributed and how many were missing. Partial sums therefore describe the available source records. Source row identifiers preserve repeated species/area labels for review. Early all-missing fields remain blank. The source’s zero values remain in the downloadable data with their coverage notes.
The GOA source ends in 2024; later GOA specifications require an update from the NOAA harvest-specification records. The 2026 BSAI specifications describe limits for an ongoing fishing year. All catch series on this page end in 2025.

title: GOA and BSAI catch and harvest specifications
text:
NOAA quota-account totals, 2013–2025
NOAA CAR110 annual catch reports provide a separate series for each region through 31 December. The parser reads each report’s published Total Catch grand total once and checks it against the sum of its area/account rows. All 26 region-year reports pass the full-year and duplicate-account checks; rounding differences are at most six metric tons.






Figure 3: NOAA CAR110 annual groundfish catch for BSAI and GOA, 2013–2025, in separate panels with vertical axes starting at zero.



The 2025 CAR110 totals are 1,774,231 metric tons for BSAI, including Community Development Quota (CDQ) catch, and 231,545 metric tons for GOA. The GOA report includes fixed-gear and trawl sablefish accounts; adding separate IFQ sablefish landings would count those catches twice. Squid accounts appear through 2018 and sculpin accounts through 2020. Subsequent NOAA ecosystem-component reports hold those categories separately.
AKFIN and CAR110 totals remain separate throughout the figures and downloads. Their differences reflect source coverage and revision dates. Older historical summaries use additional definitions and rounding conventions, so the 2003 start remains explicit.

The public website repository includes the input snapshots under data/source/. Download that ABC_TAC directory with its data/, scripts/, R/, and doc/ layout intact. Run the parsers from the archived inputs, followed by the R scripts. Each parser checks the source-file checksums before rebuilding. The Python parsers’ --refresh option retrieves new catch-report versions; the specification builder retrieves its pinned public Git revision. A later source revision requires a reviewed data update.
The data update verified 552 AKFIN table rows and 1,808 NOAA area/account rows. AKFIN species sums agree with its reported totals within two metric tons, and the two regions sum to the Alaska total within one metric ton. The harvest-specification checks reproduce 225 available measure sums from the source report and preserve 15 all-missing sums as missing.
This update prepares data summaries and figures. The linked ABC/TAC report retains its own statistical analyses, results, and model-validation status.

title: SSC minutes
text: The SSC comments app links each extracted paragraph to its original report page. The public app snapshot checked for this portal contains 4,214 stock-comment records, 43 stock labels, and 30 distinct reports, covering 2000 to 2024.

title: SSC minutes
text:
Search and check the source
Search by stock, fishery management plan (FMP), year, comment type, or text. Expand a record to read the full paragraph, then use Open page to read the source PDF.
The software matches words in the reports to assign stocks, FMPs, comment types, and model-choice labels. Some model-choice results need review. Check the original paragraph before concluding that the SSC selected a different model.
Coverage follows the reports supplied to the public app. Check each original report’s date and status when interpreting its comments.
